look_here_first: Look at the leaf dissection and overall slenderness first: lower leaves are often deeply pinnatifid, while the upper flowering branches become narrow and simple; the plant is much less gray-woolly than Verbena canescens.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: slender perennial, usually one to a few stems with an open branched flowering canopy

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: lower leaves variable but often deeply pinnately lobed or cut

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: upper leaves become much narrower, simpler, and sometimes nearly entire

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: stems comparatively sparsely hairy rather than densely gray-canescent

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: slender terminal/branched spikes with widely spaced tiny lavender-purple flowers

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: four-angled to ridged stems; opposite leaves

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: fruit breaks into four one-seeded mericarps

key_traits.label: Verbena training
key_traits.text: Separate these by leaf architecture + hair texture + spike/branching architecture before using flower color.
